patterns.T10: Gene expression: lac operon, genetic code

U1.name: Unit VI · Reproduction (16 marks)
U1.tip: Embryo sac: 7-celled, 8-nucleate. Double fertilisation = syngamy + triple fusion; endosperm (PEN) is 3n. Dioecy stops both autogamy and geitonogamy. 1 primary spermatocyte → 4 sperms. LH surge → ovulation; hCG is made only in pregnancy. ZIFT: zygote/early embryo (up to 8 blastomeres) into the fallopian tube.
U1.ncert: NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 1 Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants, Ch 2 Human Reproduction, Ch 3 Reproductive Health

U2.name: Unit VII · Genetics and Evolution (20 marks)
U2.tip: Dihybrid F₂ 9:3:3:1; test cross Tt × tt = 1:1; incomplete dominance F₂ 1:2:1. I^A, I^B co-dominant, i recessive. X-linked: carrier mother → half the sons affected. Chargaff: A = T, G = C. Hardy-Weinberg p² + 2pq + q² = 1. Lactose is the inducer of the lac operon. AUG starts; UAA, UAG, UGA stop.
U2.ncert: NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 4 Principles of Inheritance and Variation, Ch 5 Molecular Basis of Inheritance, Ch 6 Evolution

U3.name: Unit VIII · Biology and Human Welfare (12 marks)
U3.tip: Plasmodium enters as sporozoites from the female Anopheles. Antibody = H₂L₂. Ready-made antibodies (colostrum, antitoxin) = passive immunity. HIV infects helper T-cells; macrophages act as an HIV factory. High BOD = more organic matter. Methanogens (Methanobacterium) make biogas.
U3.ncert: NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 7 Human Health and Disease, Ch 8 Microbes in Human Welfare

U4.name: Unit IX · Biotechnology (12 marks)
U4.tip: EcoRI cuts GAATTC (palindrome) leaving sticky ends. DNA moves to the anode in gel electrophoresis. PCR: denaturation → annealing → extension (Taq). pBR322: insert in tetR (BamHI) → recombinants lose tetracycline resistance. RNAi against Meloidogyne incognita. First gene therapy: ADA deficiency, 1990.
U4.ncert: NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 9 Biotechnology: Principles and Processes, Ch 10 Biotechnology and its Applications

U5.name: Unit X · Ecology and Environment (10 marks)
U5.tip: Commensalism (+, 0): orchid on mango. Logistic growth dN/dt = rN(K − N)/K. About 10% of energy passes to the next trophic level. Pyramid of biomass is inverted in the sea. Evil quartet: habitat loss, over-exploitation, alien species, co-extinctions.
U5.ncert: NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 11 Organisms and Populations, Ch 12 Ecosystem, Ch 13 Biodiversity and its Conservation

questions.question: A typical mature angiosperm embryo sac is:
questions.explanation: 3 antipodals + 2 synergids + 1 egg + 1 central cell (2 polar nuclei) = 7 cells, 8 nuclei.
questions.remediation: Unit VI · Reproduction (16 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 1 Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants, Ch 2 Human Reproduction, Ch 3 Reproductive Health; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: Triple fusion in angiosperms is the fusion of:
questions.explanation: Triple fusion forms the triploid primary endosperm nucleus (PEN).
questions.remediation: Unit VI · Reproduction (16 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 1 Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants, Ch 2 Human Reproduction, Ch 3 Reproductive Health; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: Two male gametes with the egg
A male gamete with the two polar nuclei
A male gamete with the egg

questions.question: The leaf cells of a flowering plant have 24 chromosomes (2n = 24). How many chromosomes are present in a cell of its endosperm?
questions.explanation: Endosperm is triploid (3n): 3 × 12 = 36.
questions.remediation: Unit VI · Reproduction (16 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 1 Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants, Ch 2 Human Reproduction, Ch 3 Reproductive Health; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: Which outbreeding device prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy?
questions.explanation: With unisexual flowers on separate plants, neither self- nor same-plant pollination is possible.
questions.remediation: Unit VI · Reproduction (16 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 1 Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants, Ch 2 Human Reproduction, Ch 3 Reproductive Health; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: Dioecy (male and female flowers on different plants)

questions.question: How many sperms are produced from 25 primary spermatocytes?
questions.explanation: Each primary spermatocyte gives 4 spermatids/sperms after meiosis: 25 × 4 = 100.
questions.remediation: Unit VI · Reproduction (16 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 1 Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants, Ch 2 Human Reproduction, Ch 3 Reproductive Health; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: Ovulation in the human menstrual cycle is induced by:
questions.explanation: LH and FSH peak mid-cycle (about day 14); the LH surge induces rupture of the Graafian follicle.
questions.remediation: Unit VI · Reproduction (16 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 1 Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants, Ch 2 Human Reproduction, Ch 3 Reproductive Health; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: A surge of LH in the middle of the cycle
A sharp fall in FSH on day 1

questions.question: Which hormone is produced in the human body only during pregnancy?
questions.explanation: hCG, hPL and relaxin come from pregnancy; oestrogen, progesterone and LH are also made in non-pregnant women.
questions.remediation: Unit VI · Reproduction (16 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 1 Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants, Ch 2 Human Reproduction, Ch 3 Reproductive Health; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: In ZIFT, what is transferred and where?
questions.explanation: ZIFT = zygote intra fallopian transfer; >8 blastomeres → IUT; GIFT transfers ova; ICSI injects a sperm into the ovum.
questions.remediation: Unit VI · Reproduction (16 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 1 Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants, Ch 2 Human Reproduction, Ch 3 Reproductive Health; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: The zygote or early embryo (up to 8 blastomeres) into the fallopian tube
Embryos with more than 8 blastomeres into the uterus
Sperm directly into the ovum in the laboratory
Ova into the fallopian tube of another female

questions.question: In a dihybrid cross between pure round-yellow and wrinkled-green pea plants, 1600 F₂ plants are raised. How many are expected to be round-yellow?
questions.explanation: F₂ ratio 9:3:3:1, so round-yellow = 9/16 × 1600 = 900.
questions.remediation: Unit VII · Genetics and Evolution (20 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 4 Principles of Inheritance and Variation, Ch 5 Molecular Basis of Inheritance, Ch 6 Evolution; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: A tall pea plant (Tt) is crossed with a dwarf plant (tt). The expected ratio of tall to dwarf offspring is:
questions.explanation: Test cross: Tt × tt → ½ Tt (tall) : ½ tt (dwarf).
questions.remediation: Unit VII · Genetics and Evolution (20 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 4 Principles of Inheritance and Variation, Ch 5 Molecular Basis of Inheritance, Ch 6 Evolution; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: A man with blood group A (genotype I^A i) marries a woman with blood group B (I^B i). Which blood groups are possible in their children?
questions.explanation: Gametes I^A or i × I^B or i give I^A I^B (AB), I^A i (A), I^B i (B) and ii (O).
questions.remediation: Unit VII · Genetics and Evolution (20 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 4 Principles of Inheritance and Variation, Ch 5 Molecular Basis of Inheritance, Ch 6 Evolution; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: A, B and AB, but not O

questions.question: In snapdragon, a red-flowered plant (RR) is crossed with a white-flowered plant (rr). The phenotypic ratio in F₂ is:
questions.explanation: Incomplete dominance: F₁ pink (Rr); F₂ phenotype ratio equals genotype ratio 1:2:1.
questions.remediation: Unit VII · Genetics and Evolution (20 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 4 Principles of Inheritance and Variation, Ch 5 Molecular Basis of Inheritance, Ch 6 Evolution; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: A woman who is a carrier for haemophilia marries a normal man. What proportion of their sons is expected to be haemophilic?
questions.explanation: Sons get their X from the mother: half get Xʰ (affected), half get X (normal).
questions.remediation: Unit VII · Genetics and Evolution (20 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 4 Principles of Inheritance and Variation, Ch 5 Molecular Basis of Inheritance, Ch 6 Evolution; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: Down's syndrome is caused by:
questions.explanation: Down's: trisomy 21; Turner's: XO; Klinefelter's: XXY; sickle-cell: β-globin point mutation.
questions.remediation: Unit VII · Genetics and Evolution (20 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 4 Principles of Inheritance and Variation, Ch 5 Molecular Basis of Inheritance, Ch 6 Evolution; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: An extra X chromosome in males (XXY)
A point mutation in the β-globin gene

questions.question: A double-stranded DNA sample has 20% adenine. What percentage of its bases is cytosine?
questions.remediation: Unit VII · Genetics and Evolution (20 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 4 Principles of Inheritance and Variation, Ch 5 Molecular Basis of Inheritance, Ch 6 Evolution; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: In the lac operon of E. coli, the inducer is:
questions.explanation: Lactose (the substrate) binds the repressor and inactivates it, so the operon is switched on.
questions.remediation: Unit VII · Genetics and Evolution (20 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 4 Principles of Inheritance and Variation, Ch 5 Molecular Basis of Inheritance, Ch 6 Evolution; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a stop codon?
questions.explanation: AUG codes methionine and is the start codon; UAA, UAG and UGA are stop codons.
questions.remediation: Unit VII · Genetics and Evolution (20 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 4 Principles of Inheritance and Variation, Ch 5 Molecular Basis of Inheritance, Ch 6 Evolution; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: In a population in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, 16% of individuals show a recessive trait (aa). What percentage of the population is heterozygous (Aa)?
questions.remediation: Unit VII · Genetics and Evolution (20 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 4 Principles of Inheritance and Variation, Ch 5 Molecular Basis of Inheritance, Ch 6 Evolution; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: Both true; analogy = similar function, different structure (convergent evolution), which is what R describes.
questions.remediation: Unit VII · Genetics and Evolution (20 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 4 Principles of Inheritance and Variation, Ch 5 Molecular Basis of Inheritance, Ch 6 Evolution; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
questions.assertion: The wings of a butterfly and of a bird are analogous organs.
questions.reason: They perform the same function but are not anatomically similar in structure or origin.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: Plasmodium enters the human body through the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito as:
questions.explanation: Sporozoites (infectious form) are injected; they multiply in liver cells and then in RBCs.
questions.remediation: Unit VIII · Biology and Human Welfare (12 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 7 Human Health and Disease, Ch 8 Microbes in Human Welfare; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: An antibody molecule is represented as:
questions.explanation: Two heavy and two light peptide chains.
questions.remediation: Unit VIII · Biology and Human Welfare (12 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 7 Human Health and Disease, Ch 8 Microbes in Human Welfare; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: A newborn gets antibodies (IgA) from colostrum. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Ready-made antibodies are given, not produced by the baby: passive immunity.
questions.remediation: Unit VIII · Biology and Human Welfare (12 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 7 Human Health and Disease, Ch 8 Microbes in Human Welfare; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: After entering the body, HIV multiplies and attacks mainly:
questions.explanation: The decrease in helper T-cells weakens immunity, leading to opportunistic infections.
questions.remediation: Unit VIII · Biology and Human Welfare (12 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 7 Human Health and Disease, Ch 8 Microbes in Human Welfare; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: Helper T-lymphocytes, with macrophages acting as an HIV factory

questions.question: A sample of waste water has a very high BOD. This means it has:
questions.explanation: BOD measures the oxygen microbes need to oxidise organic matter; higher BOD = more polluting potential.
questions.remediation: Unit VIII · Biology and Human Welfare (12 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 7 Human Health and Disease, Ch 8 Microbes in Human Welfare; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: A large amount of organic matter, so it is highly polluting

questions.question: Biogas is produced in a biogas plant from cattle dung mainly by:
questions.explanation: Methanogens grow anaerobically on cellulose-rich material and release methane, CO₂ and H₂.
questions.remediation: Unit VIII · Biology and Human Welfare (12 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 7 Human Health and Disease, Ch 8 Microbes in Human Welfare; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: Methanogens such as Methanobacterium, under anaerobic conditions

questions.question: The recognition sequence of the restriction enzyme EcoRI is:
questions.explanation: EcoRI recognises the palindrome GAATTC and cuts between G and A, leaving sticky ends.
questions.remediation: Unit IX · Biotechnology (12 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 9 Biotechnology: Principles and Processes, Ch 10 Biotechnology and its Applications; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: During gel electrophoresis, DNA fragments move towards the:
questions.explanation: DNA is negatively charged; smaller fragments move farther through the agarose matrix.
questions.remediation: Unit IX · Biotechnology (12 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 9 Biotechnology: Principles and Processes, Ch 10 Biotechnology and its Applications; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: Anode, because DNA is negatively charged
Cathode, because DNA is positively charged

questions.question: The correct order of steps in one PCR cycle is:
questions.explanation: Heat separates strands, primers anneal, then thermostable Taq polymerase extends them.
questions.remediation: Unit IX · Biotechnology (12 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 9 Biotechnology: Principles and Processes, Ch 10 Biotechnology and its Applications; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: A gene is inserted at the BamHI site of the tetracycline-resistance gene of pBR322. Recombinant transformants will:
questions.explanation: Insertional inactivation of tetR: recombinants keep ampR but lose tetracycline resistance.
questions.remediation: Unit IX · Biotechnology (12 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 9 Biotechnology: Principles and Processes, Ch 10 Biotechnology and its Applications; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: Grow on ampicillin but not on tetracycline
Grow on tetracycline but not on ampicillin

questions.question: The first clinical gene therapy (1990) was given to a 4-year-old girl with:
questions.explanation: Functional ADA cDNA was introduced into her lymphocytes.
questions.remediation: Unit IX · Biotechnology (12 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 9 Biotechnology: Principles and Processes, Ch 10 Biotechnology and its Applications; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: Tobacco plants protected from the nematode Meloidogyne incognita by RNA interference work because:
questions.explanation: Agrobacterium vectors introduce nematode genes giving sense and anti-sense RNA; the dsRNA silences the parasite mRNA and it dies.
questions.remediation: Unit IX · Biotechnology (12 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 9 Biotechnology: Principles and Processes, Ch 10 Biotechnology and its Applications; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: dsRNA made from nematode-specific genes silences the parasite's specific mRNA
The plant produces Bt toxin that kills the nematode
The nematode's DNA is cut by EcoRI
The plant roots become too hard to infect

questions.question: An orchid growing on a mango branch, with no harm or benefit to the mango, is an example of:
questions.explanation: One species benefits (+), the other is unaffected (0).
questions.remediation: Unit X · Ecology and Environment (10 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 11 Organisms and Populations, Ch 12 Ecosystem, Ch 13 Biodiversity and its Conservation; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: A population follows logistic growth with r = 0.2 per year and carrying capacity K = 1000. At what rate (individuals per year) is it growing when N = 500?
questions.remediation: Unit X · Ecology and Environment (10 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 11 Organisms and Populations, Ch 12 Ecosystem, Ch 13 Biodiversity and its Conservation; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: Producers in an ecosystem fix 10,000 J of energy. Using the 10 per cent law, how much energy (in J) reaches the tertiary consumers?
questions.explanation: 10,000 → 1,000 (primary) → 100 (secondary) → 10 J (tertiary).
questions.remediation: Unit X · Ecology and Environment (10 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 11 Organisms and Populations, Ch 12 Ecosystem, Ch 13 Biodiversity and its Conservation; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: The pyramid of biomass in a sea is generally inverted because:
questions.explanation: Phytoplankton have a small standing biomass but reproduce fast, so consumers can outweigh them.
questions.remediation: Unit X · Ecology and Environment (10 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 11 Organisms and Populations, Ch 12 Ecosystem, Ch 13 Biodiversity and its Conservation; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: Energy flows from consumers to producers
The biomass of fishes far exceeds that of the phytoplankton at any time
Phytoplankton are absent in the sea

questions.question: Which of these is NOT one of the 'evil quartet' causes of biodiversity loss?
questions.explanation: The evil quartet: habitat loss, over-exploitation, alien species invasions, co-extinctions. Biosphere reserves are in situ conservation.
questions.remediation: Unit X · Ecology and Environment (10 marks): NCERT Biology (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 11 Organisms and Populations, Ch 12 Ecosystem, Ch 13 Biodiversity and its Conservation; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
